title: split-kernel-sm-fusion-stream-priority-sweep-2029-02
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from a week-long sweep investigating a reproducible tail-latency mode that appears when we split attention kernels into two-phase launches (split-kernel path) + enable low-priority background streams for KV cache maintenance. Goal was to understand why occupancy and SM-level active warps drop intermittently (10-30% loss) and correlate that with 95/99ms regressions in inference tail latency. This doc contains raw repro steps, Nsight capture notes, kernel timelines, hypotheses, and a short list of mitigations to test.

Context and motivation:
- Feature: split-kernel strategy introduced to reduce register pressure and allow async copies to overlap compute for long-sequence generation.
- Observed regression: p99 increases by ~15-40ms for batch sizes 1-4 in real workload when split-kernel path enabled + background stream priority set to low for cache eviction.
- Hypothesis: stream-priority interactions + kernel co-location are causing SM fusion to break (i.e., a previously continuous kernel execution is separated by small DMA/host work leading to SM preemption/eviction and inefficient warp scheduling).

HW / SW environment:
- Instance: g5.48x (A100) equivalent in our lab cluster
- Driver: NVIDIA 545.xx
- CUDA: 12.2
- Nsight Systems: 2028.11
- Build: serving-runtime@commit 2f9a7b3 (see linked PR) with split-kernel enabled behind feature flag --split_attention=true
- Runtime flags used in experiments: --batching=auto --kv-cache-maintenance-stream=1 --kv-cache-priority=low 

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start local runner with feature flag and a small synthetic workload that mimics chat completions (avg seq_len=512, finetuned Llama-variant).
2) Warm the model for 3 minutes to populate KV cache.
3) Run a constant single-request stream at 15 qps for 2 minutes while background eviction runs every 5s.
4) Capture Nsight Systems trace for the 2 minute window.

Commands used (internal):
- ./run_inference --model llama-14b-quant --port 9000 --split_attention=true --kv-cache-maintenance-stream=1 --kv-cache-priority=low --trace nsight_capture && sleep 120 && kill_trace
- nsight-sys --import capture.qdrep --report kernel-timeline.csv

High-level Nsight observations:
- Timeline shows frequent short gaps (~200-900us) between consecutive attention kernels on the primary stream (stream0) when background stream does small async copies. These gaps coincide with a visible drop in active warps per SM in the Nsight waveform.
- CUDA graph capture behaves differently: when we record the attention sequence into a CUDA graph (graphify), gaps vanish in the trace but tail-latency can still spike after graph replay if eviction happens during the graph's hanging phase.
- Kernel magnitudes: attention_fwd_split_k0 and attention_fwd_split_k1 have combined avg durations similar to monolithic attention kernel; but scheduling shifts lead to increased kernel launch overhead and less effective tensor-core utilization for k1 when it starts after a short gap.

Numerical snippets from trace (representative):
- avg active warps / SM during steady run: 22 -> drops to 16 at gap points (~27% loss)
- occupancy reported by profiler for k0: 0.68, for k1: 0.52 (k1 lower due to register reuse differences)
- kernel latency: k0 320us, gap 420us, k1 410us vs monolithic_k 740us (monolithic has slightly better fused tensor-core utilization)

Detailed timeline notes:
- 00:00 baseline: continuous k0->k1 w/ <50us gap when background stream idle.
- 00:23 first spike: background stream issues a small device->device async copy (4KB), NS records stream preemption marker; active warp occupancy dips and k1's achieved tensor-core utilization drops by ~18%.
- 00:27 repeated pattern: each eviction/maintenance event introduces a scheduling boundary; the hardware seems to prefer quiescing some warps before accepting the higher latency kernel launch on stream0.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stream priority + small async copies introduce micro-preemptions that cause SM-level scheduling regrouping. Regrouping harms tensor-core steady-state and reduces achieved occupancy for the follow-up split kernel.
2) CUDA graph replay hides launch overhead but leaves the runtime in a state where subsequent eviction reorders memory residency, causing unexpected page/segment migration stalls for k1 (more likely when mixed memory pools used).
3) Split kernel increases register pressure across the two kernels in a way that the second kernel has fewer resident blocks and lower occupancy; combined with preemption this effect is amplified.

Experiments run and quick results:
- EXP-A: disable background stream (eviction on same stream) -> tail latency returns to baseline, occupancy recovers.
- EXP-B: raise background priority to medium -> gap frequency drops ~70%, p99 improves but cost/latency tradeoff increases.
- EXP-C: enable CUDA graph capture for recurring generation loop -> per-inference jitter reduced but occasional spike remains correlated with host-side GC in our Python worker (opened separate ticket).
- EXP-D: fuse split kernel back into single kernel (compile flag) -> best tail latency, but regressed peak memory use by ~8%.

Immediate mitigations to try (short list):
- Introduce a tiny spin-synchronization (micro-yield) on the maintenance stream to avoid overlapping async copies with the critical k0->k1 boundary (cheap software mitigation).
- Keep split-kernel as compile-time opt but add runtime heuristic: if maintenance stream had activity in last 1ms, force monolithic path for the next n inferences.
- Adjust nvtx labeling to ensure Nsight markers for preemption points are visible (helpful for future capture triage).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is this behavior driver-specific (different drivers/firmware modulate preemption threshold)? Need cross-driver sweep.
- Are we seeing any interaction with peer-to-peer NVLink traffic (some captures show NCCL activity coincidentally)? Should reproduce with NCCL disabled.
- What is the additional cost of always favoring monolithic kernel for tail-sensitive customers? Need cost/throughput tradeoff experiment.

Next steps / experiments planned:
- Cross-driver validation (545.xx, 555.xx) by 2029-02-20 (assigned to Diego).
- Add micro-yield patch to runtime and A/B test 24h in canary fleet (Ravi).
- Re-run captures with NCCL disabled and with P2P traffic injected to see amplification (Anika).

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add ticket to infra to collect periodic Nsight captures in canary region on 2 separate driver versions.
- Create a lightweight perf test that toggles split vs monolithic per-request to quantify cost delta in production workloads.
- Document observed occupancy delta in a confluence page (link placeholder).

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducer capture
- warmup 3min -> capture 2min -> annotate with NVTX before k0 and after k1 -> include device memory snapshot at start/end -> export timeline as csv -> post to /perf/traces with run id

Attach: linked artifacts above (Jira + PR + Slack thread).

If anything obvious missing, tag me in the Slack thread and I'll paste the raw qdrep for someone to inspect.
